## Loading Libraries
```{python}
import polars as pl
import pandas as pd
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns import apriori
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns import association_rules
```

## Load and Discretize Data
```{python}
data = pl.read_csv("Gaming and Mental Health.csv")

# Step 1: Pick categorical columns or discretize numeric columns
data_discrete = data.with_columns([

    pl.when(pl.col("age") < 18).then(pl.lit("Under 18"))
      .when(pl.col("age") < 25).then(pl.lit("18-24"))
      .when(pl.col("age") < 35).then(pl.lit("25-34"))
      .otherwise(pl.lit("35+"))
      .alias("age_group"),

    pl.when(pl.col("daily_gaming_hours") < 2).then(pl.lit("Low Gaming"))
      .when(pl.col("daily_gaming_hours") < 5).then(pl.lit("Moderate Gaming"))
      .otherwise(pl.lit("High Gaming"))
      .alias("gaming_level"),

    pl.when(pl.col("sleep_hours") < 6).then(pl.lit("Poor Sleep"))
      .when(pl.col("sleep_hours") < 8).then(pl.lit("Adequate Sleep"))
      .otherwise(pl.lit("Good Sleep"))
      .alias("sleep_quality"),

    pl.when(pl.col("social_isolation_score") < 3).then(pl.lit("Low Isolation"))
      .when(pl.col("social_isolation_score") < 7).then(pl.lit("Moderate Isolation"))
      .otherwise(pl.lit("High Isolation"))
      .alias("isolation_level"),

    # Keep these categorical columns as-is
    pl.col("gaming_addiction_risk_level"),
    pl.col("mood_state"),
    pl.col("mood_swing_frequency"),
])

# Select only the discretized columns for association rules
cols = ["age_group", "gaming_level", "sleep_quality", "isolation_level",
        "gaming_addiction_risk_level", "mood_state", "mood_swing_frequency"]

data_discrete = data_discrete.select(cols).drop_nulls()
print(data_discrete.shape)
data_discrete.head()
```

## One-Hot Encode for Apriori
```{python}
# One-hot encode all columns (to_dummies creates col_value columns)
data_dummies = data_discrete.to_dummies()
data_pd = data_dummies.to_pandas()

print(f"Shape after encoding: {data_pd.shape}")
data_pd.head()
```

## Step 2: Run Apriori
```{python}
frequent_itemsets = apriori(data_pd, min_support=0.3, use_colnames=True)
frequent_itemsets = frequent_itemsets.sort_values("support", ascending=False)
print(f"Number of frequent itemsets: {len(frequent_itemsets)}")
frequent_itemsets.head(10)
```

## Step 3: Generate Association Rules
```{python}
rules = association_rules(frequent_itemsets, metric="lift", min_threshold=1.0)

# Clean up for readability
rules['antecedents'] = rules['antecedents'].apply(lambda x: tuple(x))
rules['consequents'] = rules['consequents'].apply(lambda x: tuple(x))
rules["antecedent_len"] = rules["antecedents"].apply(lambda x: len(x))

rules_sorted = rules.sort_values("lift", ascending=False)
print(f"Total rules generated: {len(rules_sorted)}")
rules_sorted.head(20)
```

## Step 4: Inspect Interesting Patterns by Lift
```{python}
# Filter for strong, meaningful rules
interesting_rules = rules[
    (rules["antecedent_len"] >= 1) &
    (rules["confidence"] > 0.6) &
    (rules["lift"] > 1.5)
].sort_values("lift", ascending=False)

print(f"Interesting rules (confidence > 0.6, lift > 1.5): {len(interesting_rules)}")
interesting_rules[["antecedents", "consequents", "support", "confidence", "lift"]].head(15)
```

## Interpretation
```{python}
# Display top 5 rules for interpretation
top5 = rules_sorted[["antecedents", "consequents", "support", "confidence", "lift"]].head(5)
print("Top 5 Rules by Lift:\n")
for _, row in top5.iterrows():
    print(f"  {row['antecedents']} --> {row['consequents']}")
    print(f"    Support: {row['support']:.3f} | Confidence: {row['confidence']:.3f} | Lift: {row['lift']:.3f}")
    print()

```

Interpretation:

- All top 5 rules center on three co-occurring attributes: High Gaming, Poor Sleep, and the 18-24 age group.

- Rule 1 (Lift = 1.382): Players with Poor Sleep AND Moderate Isolation are 1.38x more likely than chance to also be High Gamers, with 88.6% confidence — the strongest rule found.

- Rule 3 (Lift = 1.349): Among High Gamers aged 18-24, Poor Sleep follows 80.3% of the time, suggesting young heavy gamers disproportionately sacrifice sleep.

- Lift values (~1.35–1.38) indicate moderate but consistent associations — these patterns are real but not extreme, suggesting gaming behavior, sleep quality, and age cluster together meaningfully.

- Notably, addiction risk and mood state did not surface in the top rules, suggesting these variables may be more uniformly distributed or require a lower min_support threshold to reveal associations.
